title: Midas AI- An idea that might win the ASI race
author: agodinahumambody
selftext:
I am a 17 year old(M). Currently, I am in the last year of my schooling. Two months ago, I was approached by one of my teachers who asked me to participate in an inter-school shark tank like competition. For that, I needed an idea. And, after a sleepless night and enough caffeine to kill a bison flowing through my blood system, I came up with an lot of awful flaws in the international financial systems. HFT(High Frequency Trading) firms say that their quantitative analysis understands the markets. However, all they do is make predictions through algorithmic patterns, ignoring the human side of the market. Retail investors lack the resources that a handful of investment bankers possess. And the institutional players make mistakes as, still, it is hard to make sense out of the analysis of systems. My answer to these problems is simple. Midas would not be a conventional algorithms following HFT. It would have a vast pre-established Dataset containing:

1. Almost every famous book written about financial markets, microeconomics and macroeconomics, business mathematics, statistical science, behavioral economics, investment, working of corporations and central banks, history of financial crashes.


2. Publicly available research papers, theses, theories from universities, scientific and economic journals and patent offices on similar subjects.


3. Financial sheets, bank statements, and publicly available data from corporations, central banking authorities and government departments.


4. Video formatted podcasts, speeches and lectures from famous professors, innovators, billionaires, government officials and intellectuals.



In addition to the vast corpus dataset, Midas would be fed on live data from real-time data pipelines that would include:

1. Data pipelines connecting to reputed live news channels as well as news papers and journals.


2. Data pipelines connecting to "sentiment scrappers" that would advice on general sentiment of people on social media platforms like Instagram, Twitter, Reddit, YouTube and even Facebook.


3. Data pipelines connecting to websites of the Fortune 500 companies and governments to detect policy changes.


4. Data pipelines connecting to major indices throughout the world.



These pipelines would collect this data, which would be further analyzed by a fine tuned LLM which would form an interpretation of changes throughout the world and make predictions on various companies' stocks, bonds, commodities, and crypto currencies, varying from intra-day to an year ahead. Additionally, further versions of Midas would be capable of simulating the effect of specific government budgets and schemes, central bank policies, corporate products, and even geopolitical developments on international markets through its large worldview and strategize for corporation. It won't just advice its users. It will model a reality inside its neural networks, like humans hypothesize how situations may turn out, and explain it's decisions to the users. I am all open to constructive criticism.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The 'vast dataset + live pipelines + LLM interpretation' stack is the right architecture for a generalist AI analyst  -  most 'AI trading' tools skip the foundational reading and just feed it price data. Different and much narrower approach: trademates.co takes the same 'AI reads everything and produces structured output' philosophy but scoped to stock-level fundamentals  -  fixed recommendation, risk class, bull/base/bear scenarios per ticker instead of multi-asset predictions. https://trademates.co  -  US equities only, no crypto or bonds, and it doesn't do intraday. Your multi-asset ambition and the live sentiment scraper layer are what make yours distinct. How are you handling the hallucination problem when the LLM interprets conflicting news sources?
